questions.question: Analyze howdirect, early reflections, and reverb contributes to a sense / of envelopment and spaciousness.
questions.solution_html:
• Direct Sound, Early Reflections, and Reverberation
  • • Direct sound provides clarity and localization.
  • • Early reflections (10–50 ms) enhance intimacy.
  • • Reverberation adds spaciousness and envelopment.
  • • Balanced reflections produce natural, immersive sound.
  • • Excess reflections cause muddiness; insufficient ones cause dryness.
questions.final_answer: • Excess reflections cause muddiness; insufficient ones cause dryness
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss practical applications of SPL measurement in real-world / contexts such as workplace safety, environmental noise monitoring, and audio system calibration. Give examples of how measurements guide decisions.
questions.solution_html:
• Applications of SPL Measurement
  • • Workplace safety: maintain levels below 85 dB.
  • • Environmental monitoring: control traffic/industrial noise.
  • • System calibration and equalization in audio setups.
  • • SPL meters use A-weighting to reflect human sensitivity.
questions.final_answer: Option weighting to reflect human sensitivity.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Evaluate the differences in reverberation time requirements between / small spaces /monitoring rooms, listening rooms) and large spaces . How does RT affect clarity, warmth, and adaptability in these environments?
questions.solution_html:
• Reverberation in Small vs Large Spaces
  • • Small rooms: short RT (0.3–0.6 s) for clarity.
  • • Large halls: longer RT (1.8–2.5 s) for warmth and blend.
  • • Long RT harms speech intelligibility.
  • • Short RT reduces musical richness.
  • • Multipurpose halls use variable acoustic panels.
questions.final_answer: • Multipurpose halls use variable acoustic panels
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
